item.title: 🎭 The good reason is cover for the real one
item.description:
J. P. Morgan gets credited with a blunt line: a man has two reasons for doing something, a good reason and the real reason. The attribution arrives late (Owen Wister, 1930), and the saying was already loose in the air.

The good reason is for the room

When you quit a job, take a deal, or pick a side in an argument, you usually lead with the version that sounds fair, practical, or kind. That acceptable reason travels well: it lowers conflict, protects reputation, and gives other people a story they can nod at without digging.

item.title: 🎭 The deniability hood: why groups prefer not to know
item.description:
In The Elephant in the Brain, Kevin Simler and Robin Hanson argue that human behavior is driven by hidden motives we rarely acknowledge, even to ourselves. The paradox sounds wrong at first: shouldn’t ignorance be most useful when it is hidden?

What they said

It’s never useful to have secret gaps in your knowledge, or to adopt false beliefs that you keep entirely to yourself. The entire value of strategic ignorance and related phenomena lies in the way others act when they believe that you’re ignorant. Ignorance is at its most useful when it is most public.
